To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Phanerozioic history of geomagnetic polarity reversals and the time dependent growth of the inner core are controlled by time variable heat flux at the CMB, which is driven by mantle convection, and by changes of inner core size, which are controlled by inner core chemical buoyant flow.
geomagnetic reversal rate and core growth history are sensitive to the history of CMB heat transfer and that these histories are determined by mantle convection.
the Phanerozic evolution of the geomagnetic field is controlled by the evolution of mantle convection and the core.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the connections between the geomagnetic polarity reversal frequency, core dynamics and evolution, and mantle dynamics through Phanerozioic time.
the interconnections between geomagnetic polarity reversals, core evolution and mantle convection.
the evolution of the core and mantle over Phanerozo time and how this influences the evolution of the geomagnetic field and its reversals.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the geomagnetic field has a complex history, which is controlled by the evolution of the Earth's mantle, core, and the coupling between them.
the Phanerozic geomagnetic field is controlled by mantle convection, and the evolution of the geomagnetic field and reversal rate are controlled by the evolution of the core.

the Phanerozic history of geomagnetic field structure and reversal statistics are sensitive to the details of the thermal history of the Earth, including the time evolution of CMB heat loss, inner core size and growth, and rotation history.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dynamo is sensitive to CMB heat flux, and the dynamo with the variable CMB heatflux is more sensitive to the history of mantle convection than the dynamo with constant CMB heatflux.
geomagnetic reversals are a consequence of the dynamo, but the frequency and structure of geomagnetic reversals is controlled by the thermal evolution of Earth's core.
a time independent heat flux at the base of the Earth's liquid core cannot produce the time dependence of the geomagnetic reversal rate and field structure seen in the geologic record.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the time variability of CMMB heat flux, which is a proxy for the time evolution of the core and mantle, is the dominant control on reversal frequency, and that reversal frequency is only weakly dependent on the time evolution of other dynamo control parameters.
the evolution of the core and the lower mantle is strongly coupled and the geomagnetic field and the core evolve together with the lower mantle.
the Phanerozic history of the Earth's core can be constrained by the geomagnetic reversal record and the present day magnetic field structure.
